title: Client filter defaults: rest at nothing chosen, scope All to the signed-in person's stakeholder projects, remember each person's choice

approvals.evidence: Stated by the CEO in the Claude Code session ("Approved", 2026-09-05) after the intent-stage summary. The 13 open questions, including OQ1 (the stakeholder definition, which blocks AC2, AC5, AC14-AC16), were not answered at approval; the implementation planner must surface OQ1 before any step that depends on it.

OQ1 answered in the Claude Code session: "stakeholder means live ProjectMember row" (definition d of OQ1). Version 2 records it as BR8 and retires AC14 and AC16, which were conditional on definitions a and b.

OQ3, OQ4, OQ10 and OQ11 answered in the Claude Code session on 2026-09-05: scoped-All narrows both the Client dropdown and the rows; an explicit client choice is scoped too; unresolved actors see nothing; exempt seats get the same scoped All while access is unchanged; records with no project-tier ancestor stay in. Recorded as BR9-BR12; version 3 supersedes version 2.

OQ5, OQ8 and OQ9 answered in the Claude Code session on 2026-09-05: the chosen client persists per person on the operating model; Clear and saved views return to the person's choice and reveal switches for the reveal only; report figures under scoped-All count only the person's projects and say so. Recorded as BR13-BR15; version 4 supersedes version 3. Every question that blocked a plan step is now answered.

body.problem: The issue workspace opens with the Client filter at 'All' (EMPTY_FILTERS.client in lib/types.ts:384; components/IssueWorkspace.tsx:621 seeds state from it), so a signed-in person sees every client's work in the payload they receive before choosing anything, and the Clear button (components/FilterBar.tsx:286) and the reveal-a-hidden-row path (IssueWorkspace.tsx:992) both return to that same view. Nishant Sekhar asked on 2026-08-17 (docs/pending-actions.md D1, A4) for three changes: (1) the Client filter rests at None rather than every client; (2) choosing All shows only the projects on which the signed-in person is a stakeholder, not every project in the firm; (3) each person picks their own project and the choice persists for them. Two facts read from the code on 2026-09-05 change the shape of the request without resolving it. First, part (2) is already true for every non-exempt internal seat: since the project-membership design of 2026-08-24, redactForReader (lib/db/boot.ts:418) applies projectView(memberProjectIdsFor(state, mine)) so a non-member project never reaches the browser; the exemption for ROLE_ADMIN and the machine actor (isExempt, lib/access.ts:407) and records with no project-tier ancestor are the only places where All still shows the whole firm. D1 was written a week before that design and was never reconciled against it. Second, the control is client-tier (it compares issue.client, the nearest external-party ancestor's name; facetsOf lib/tree.ts:351) while every candidate meaning of stakeholder is project- or engagement-tier, so on this control 'All shows my projects' can only mean 'list the clients under which I hold at least one stakeholder project'. The request cannot be built as stated because 'stakeholder' has no single computable meaning in the data (see open_questions OQ1) and because no per-person persisted preference for a filter exists (saved views are deliberately the team's, lib/savedViews.ts; viewChoice and panel layout are per browser).

source.reference: docs/pending-actions.md rows D1 and A4 (Nishant Sekhar, 2026-08-17; document last edited 2026-08-23, commit b4d5b3b). Code observations dated 2026-09-05 are cited file:line in the criteria and rules; inferences by the analysts are marked E3 where they occur.

scope_in: The Client control in the issue workspace (Tree, Board and Calendar, the views FiltersHeader mounts; My work, Portfolio and the record views are untouched) rests at a value meaning 'nothing chosen' for a person who has not yet chosen, instead of 'All'.

A person-relative reading of All: the clients listed and the rows shown are limited to projects on which the signed-in person (directoryPersonFor(model, actor), resolved server-side) is a stakeholder, per a definition the product owner fixes in OQ1.
Each signed-in person can choose a client (or a project, see OQ6) and that choice is restored for that person on their next visit, in the persistence scope fixed by OQ5.
The reset paths that return to 'All' today (Clear, revealIssue) and the report scope label (scopeLabel, openClientPack) are made consistent with the new resting state.
Client-seat behaviour (Person.clientScopeId, clientView, scenario GA1) is preserved unchanged.
scope_out: Any change to the client-seat boundary (Person.clientScopeId, clientView, GA1). This request is about internal seats' default view.

Any change to what a person may DO on a project (can(), lib/access.ts) or to the project read gate (redactForReader, projectView, isExempt in lib/db/boot.ts). Stakeholder-scoping is a view default, not a permission; if the product owner intends it as access control, that is a permission-model change and a different requirement.
Changing Allocation, ProjectMember or Engagement semantics to make one of them mean 'stakeholder'. The definition is chosen among what exists or declared new; the data models are not bent to fit.
Converting saved views (lib/savedViews.ts) to per-person. The saved-views design of 2026-08-31 lists personal-only views as a non-goal; reversing that needs its own ADR.
D2, the issue-type taxonomy, which shares the same pending-actions section but is a separate modelling decision.
Portfolio and My work views, which compute their own lists and ignore record filters.

acceptance_criteria.given: a signed-in internal person for whom no client or project choice has been recorded
acceptance_criteria.when: the issue workspace loads on the Tree, Board or Calendar view
acceptance_criteria.then: the Client control shows the 'nothing chosen' state with an instructing caption (not 'Client: All' and not the bare word 'None'), no issue rows are listed, the grid shows a one-line prompt naming the next action, the counts strip still reports the full total the way hidden-completed records are counted today, and the Filters chip does not count the resting value as an active filter. [E3 on the empty grid; conditional on OQ2]

acceptance_criteria.given: the signed-in person resolves via directoryPersonFor to a directory Person who is a stakeholder on project P1 and not on project P2 under the OQ1 definition, and is not exempt from the project read gate
acceptance_criteria.then: issues whose project-tier ancestor (found through tiersOf, not a literal kind) is P1 are listed and issues under P2 are not, and the Client dropdown offers only clients that have at least one project the person is a stakeholder on. For a non-exempt seat under definition (d) ProjectMember this already holds through the read gate; the criterion then verifies that the filter agrees with the payload rather than computing a second, different set. [conditional on OQ1, OQ3]

acceptance_criteria.given: the person resolves but is a stakeholder on no project under the OQ1 definition
acceptance_criteria.then: the view is empty and a message states why in the codebase's teaching-message convention, distinguishable from the boot banner's 'not staffed on any project' note, and the view is NOT widened to every project. [E3, mirrors GA1's deny-by-default]

acceptance_criteria.given: the signed-in actor does not resolve to a directory Person (the fallback-role case, lib/access.ts:348-360)
acceptance_criteria.then: the outcome is the same empty-with-reason state as AC3, never every project. [E3; conditional on OQ10]

acceptance_criteria.given: the person picks a single client X from the dropdown
acceptance_criteria.then: the rows shown are those with issue.client === X AND, per OQ4, either every project under X or only X's projects the person is a stakeholder on. [conditional on OQ4]

acceptance_criteria.given: person A chose client or project P and the choice was recorded
acceptance_criteria.when: A opens the workspace again within the persistence scope fixed by OQ5
acceptance_criteria.then: the Client control shows P and the rows are filtered to P without A choosing again. [conditional on OQ5, OQ6]

acceptance_criteria.given: person A has chosen P1 and person B, in the same tenant, chooses P2
acceptance_criteria.then: A sees P1; B's choice never changes A's; neither choice appears in the shared saved-views list (lib/savedViews.ts) and neither is disclosed to a client seat through clientView. [E3 on saved views]

acceptance_criteria.given: the same person has seats in two tenants
acceptance_criteria.then: the choice restored is the one recorded for that tenant, and a node id from the other tenant is never applied: an unknown id degrades to 'nothing chosen', never to All, following parseSavedFilters' fail-closed discipline. [E3]
client returns to the person's recorded choice if one exists, else to 'nothing chosen', never to unscoped All. [E3; conditional on OQ8]

acceptance_criteria.given: a person follows a notification, search hit or My-work row to an issue outside the currently filtered set (revealIssue, IssueWorkspace.tsx:985-996, today resets to EMPTY_FILTERS and toasts 'Filters cleared')
acceptance_criteria.when: the issue's project is inside the person's stakeholder set
acceptance_criteria.then: filters widen to scoped-All (or to the record's own client, per OQ8) and the issue is revealed; when it is outside, the row is not revealed and the notice says why, rather than resetting to a state that hides everything. [E3; conditional on OQ8]

acceptance_criteria.given: a client-role seat with Person.clientScopeId set, or an unattached client seat
acceptance_criteria.then: the clientView boundary applies exactly as today: the attached seat never sees anything outside its client and the unattached seat stays empty. Cite clientView(state, clientScopeId), not a new gate.

acceptance_criteria.given: a saved view whose filters.client is 'All' (any view saved before this change) or that was saved while the client rested at 'nothing chosen'
acceptance_criteria.then: 'All' is read as the person-relative All of AC2, and the resting sentinel is either excluded on save or applying it is defined, so a shared view never applies an empty grid by accident. [E3; conditional on OQ8]

acceptance_criteria.given: the Client control is at 'nothing chosen' or scoped-All
acceptance_criteria.when: the Daily IMS or a client pack is exported
acceptance_criteria.then: scopeLabel does not print 'All clients - <org>'; it states the actual scope, and openClientPack refuses 'nothing chosen' with the same teaching message it uses for 'All' today (IssueWorkspace.tsx:1779-1782). Whether position figures count the whole workspace or only the person's projects is OQ9. [E3]

acceptance_criteria.given: a ProjectMember row on project P for the signed-in person with removedAt set, and another on project Q with removedAt null
acceptance_criteria.then: P is out of the stakeholder set and Q is in, whatever the project role on either row; the same rows the read gate consults produce the same answer here

acceptance_criteria.given: a ROLE_ADMIN holder or the machine actor, exempt from the project read gate
acceptance_criteria.then: the outcome is whichever OQ11 fixes: the filter narrows to their stakeholder set while the payload stays whole (a display default, not an access change), or All stays the whole firm for exempt seats. Either way isExempt and redactForReader are not modified. [conditional on OQ11]

business_rules: BR1. 'Stakeholder' is computed in exactly one pure function of (WorkspaceState, resolved personId, and 'today' as a parameter if the definition is date-bounded), never by display name alone; the UI, reports and scenarios all read that one function. If OQ1 lands on ProjectMember, that function is memberProjectIdsFor (lib/projectBoundary.ts:88), not a second definition beside it.

BR2. Deny by default: an unresolved person, an unattached seat, or a person on no project sees an empty scoped view with a reason, never a widened one; the rule GA1 fixes for client seats is applied to the new default for internal seats.
BR3. The stakeholder set is derived at read and never stored (derived-never-stored); only the person's own choice, a stated preference, is stored, as a node id rather than a client name.
BR4. A person's choice is a per-person fact keyed by directory personId and tenant. It is not a saved view (those are the team's by design) and is never visible to, or applied to, anyone else.

BR5. Any new write path that records a person's choice resolves personId at write, as CLAUDE.md's resource-model note requires of every write path, and refuses rather than storing a name-only record; the actor is passed in from the sealed session, never taken from the request body.

BR6. Tenant isolation holds at both layers: the stakeholder computation reads only the actor's tenant (every collection involved already loads under withTenant()), and a stored choice is keyed by tenant.

BR7. 'Nothing chosen' on the Client facet is a typed sentinel on FilterState that cannot be confused with the discipline facet's 'None' ('records without a discipline', lib/tree.ts:389-394). Same word to the requester, different meaning; the code must not share the token, and every consumer that today compares to the literal 'All' (FilterDropdown's on-accent, FiltersHeader's activeCount, matchesFilters, visibleRows, scopeLabel, revealIssue) compares to the resting value instead.
BR8. The client-seat boundary (clientView) and the project read gate (redactForReader, projectView, isExempt) are applied before any filter default and are never widened or narrowed by this feature.
BR9. Nothing here changes what a person may do; can(model, actor, key) is untouched. Visibility by stakeholder is a default view, not an authorisation.

BR10. Allocation stays a capacity fact and ProjectMember stays an access fact (CLAUDE.md resource model). If OQ1 chooses Allocation, the filter reads it and never writes it; choosing one candidate never creates or implies a record of another kind.

BR8 (OQ1 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). A person is a stakeholder on a project if and only if they hold a live ProjectMember row on it: personId matches, removedAt is null. Project role is not a filter. Allocation, engagement naming and SOW naming do not confer stakeholder status. This is the definition the project read gate already uses (lib/projectBoundary.ts), so "All shows my projects" for non-exempt seats reuses it rather than adding a second notion of stakeholder.

BR9 (OQ3 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). Scoped-All narrows both: the Client dropdown lists only clients where the signed-in person holds at least one stakeholder project (BR8), and the rows under All are only issues whose project-tier ancestor is a stakeholder project.

BR10 (OQ4 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). An explicit client choice is scoped the same way: rows are that client's stakeholder projects only. Scoping is a property of the person's view, not of the All option.

BR11 (OQ10 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). A signed-in actor who does not resolve to a directory Person has no stakeholder projects: All shows no rows and the dropdown is empty, with a caption saying the account is not in the directory. The unscoped fallback view is retired for the filter.

BR12 (OQ11 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). Exempt seats (ROLE_ADMIN, the machine actor) get the same scoped All as everyone; their access is unchanged and any client remains choosable. Records with no project-tier ancestor, which the membership design leaves ungated, stay in under All.

BR13 (OQ5 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). The person's chosen client is a stated preference stored on the operating model as a per-person map keyed by directory personId, in the notificationPrefs shape: one reducer arm, one ACTION_PERMISSIONS row, SHAPES and KINDS entries, attributed and audited, no Prisma migration. It follows the person across devices. The browser-local form is rejected (ADR 0002 alternative).

BR14 (OQ8 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). Clear returns the filter to the person's stored choice, or to nothing chosen when there is none. Revealing an issue from elsewhere switches the client to that issue's client for the duration of the reveal and does not alter the stored choice. A saved view captured at the resting state stores no client; applying any saved view leaves the person's choice in place.

BR15 (OQ9 resolved, E1, Nishant Sekhar 2026-09-05). Under scoped-All the report figures, including the Daily IMS position, count only the person's stakeholder projects, and the report header names that scope in place of "All clients". A report never states a scope wider than the rows it was computed from.
domain_entities: IssueDetail.client (free-text client name the filter compares; lib/tree.ts matchesFilters 383-400, visibleRows 461-495, facetsOf 351)
ScheduleRow kind/parentId chain and NODE_KINDS client | engagement | project via tiersOf (the control is at the client tier, the scoping at the project tier)
Allocation (prisma/schema.prisma:622; lib/capacity.ts:234): projectId, optional personId, startDate/endDate, percentage, deletedAt

ProjectMember and DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROLES incl. PROJROLE_SPONSOR, PROJROLE_CUSTOMER, PROJROLE_STAKEHOLDER (lib/staffing.ts; prisma/schema.prisma:652); memberProjectIdsFor and projectView (lib/projectBoundary.ts)
Engagement.engagementLeader / projectManager / clientSponsor (prisma/schema.prisma:543-546; lib/engagement.ts:49-52): free-text names, no personId, engagement tier

SavedView and parseSavedFilters (lib/savedViews.ts); model.notificationPrefs and setNotificationPref (lib/workspace.ts:5810) as the per-person preference precedent; viewChoice (lib/viewChoice.ts) as the per-browser precedent
open_questions: OQ2. What does 'None' show: an empty grid until a choice is made (the E3 reading used in AC1), or the person's last choice, with 'nothing chosen' only ever seen on first use? If a choice persists (part 3), parts 1 and 3 are one behaviour, not two.

OQ6. 'Each person picks their own project': the Client control has no project level and facetsOf has no project facet. Is a Project control being asked for (an addition to the filter bar, a Principle 10 check), or is 'project' here the client? If a project control, which tier when the organisation's chain is configured differently from the default?

OQ7. People whose role makes them accountable for everything (Platform Administrator; Engagement Leader, which G7 records as carrying all 38 permissions) but who hold no allocation and no membership: do they see nothing under All? BR2 says yes unless the definition says otherwise; the membership design already names the engagement leader as its known limitation.

OQ12. Was scripts/backfill-project-members.ts --commit run against production, and when? docs/verification-checklist.md has no entry. If OQ1 lands on ProjectMember and the backfill was not run, every non-exempt internal seat is already seeing an empty tree today, which would be a live defect, not a feature gap.

OQ13. Priority. The requester did not state a band. P2 is entered here only because the schema requires a value and the canonical-model definition of P2 ('real, but belongs to a named person or a named date') matches A4's standing as an item waiting on one answer from the product owner; it is the analyst's placeholder (E3), to be confirmed or changed at Gate 1.
